exemption.reason: Not reviewed, and deliberately so: this is the first mapping of pp. 16-18, written as the mapping step of #434, and no second reading has been run. Recording anything else would claim a review this map has not. `legacy` is the wrong word and is used for the reason examples/srd-52-playing-the-game/review.json, examples/frcp-6-12-81/review.json and examples/hazmat-172-table/review.json already record: it is the only exemption kind that names a tracking issue, and `non-semantic` needs a reviewed map to depart from, which a first mapping does not have. The map was trial evidence used for nothing downstream until #446: it now declares a `map-package.json`, and nothing consumes it yet. A second reading should look hardest at seven things. Whether `bloodied`'s threshold is genuinely open: the map says the corpus does not settle whether 'half your Hit Points' is half the maximum or half the current total, and 0065 rules that it is the maximum -- a reading a second mapper may find obvious enough that the entry should have been `clear`, or open enough that it should have been `unresolved`. Whether `hit-point-maximum` is honestly one entry: its quote ends mid-sentence because the extraction puts the whole Resting section, the folio and the running head between the sentence's halves, and `split-by-sidebar` is the closest value in 0024's closed set to a defect that is not a sidebar at all. Whether the three entries that split one printed paragraph into separate rules -- p. 16's Hit Points paragraph into four, the Damage Rolls paragraph into five, and p. 18's Death Saving Throws run-on into two -- cut the corpus where the corpus cuts itself, or where an implementer would. Whether the two declined entries decline advice or drop rules: `character-demise` is what a player does after a character dies, and `damage-dice-are-stated-elsewhere` is a sentence that exists only to point. Whether `spell-damage-dice` is rightly the map's one assertion -- the corpus says a spell supplies the dice and the modifiers and states neither, which is the shape of an assertion, but it could as well have been a value with an unmapped cross-reference. Whether the six draws are the six the corpus makes, and in particular whether `damage-against-multiple-targets` is right to declare a draw it does not itself roll, on the ground that the rule is about how many rolls there are. And whether this map's vocabulary is the right eight terms: `Hit Point maximum` and `Death Saving Throw` are phrases the chapter uses constantly, and admitting them generated 22 of the map's term pointers.
